source_review: The two sorted-list lemmas concern genuine real lists with multiplicities, so ties are retained. The literal median is index7 of exactly15 sorted distances; the length proof excludes the getD fallback, mergeSort preserves countP, and duplicate-free finRange indices connect list multiplicities to the actual Finset of copy indices. At least8 distances below b imply median<=b, and the actual median ball always contains8 copies. The strict-less fold scan from index0 is the actual chooseCopy implementation and minimizes all15 scores; this does not overclaim a separate tie-position classification theorem. The physical represented-Frobenius coefficientDistance is a pseudometric, with symmetry/triangle sufficient even for dependent generators. Any two8-element subsets of Fin15 intersect, giving actual postprocess distance<=3rho from an explicit eight-good coefficient event about a fixed center, including radius0. The center is used only in analysis and is not given to the algorithm. For the relative theorem, the attained Pythagorean center converts the literal eight-copy squared-error premise at squaredAccuracy(epsilon)=epsilon/9 into radius sqrt((epsilon/9)*OPT^2). The3rho conclusion yields actual squared error<=(1+epsilon)*OPT^2 and hence the required norm error<=(1+epsilon)*OPT for epsilon>=0. There is no division by OPT and no nonzero-OPT premise, so the zero optimum case is retained; the expanded consumer checks actual exact membership. The schedule and response list are arbitrary, and postprocess is the unchanged literal model function. The eight-good cardinality remains an explicit hypothesis; its probability is not proved by this scope.
